title: Peder Vibe to Peder Juel, Danish resident in Stockholm, 1651-1655, cipher passages in the new alphabet ("ny Alphabet") of 11 letters or pages (part of catalogue 2527, Rigsarkivet TKUA Sverige): shift-per-word alphabet and opener table recovered from a gloss of the time, nomenclator open: read in part

documents.shelfmark: Copenhagen, Rigsarkivet, TKUA, Speciel del, Sverige, Resident Peder Juels og Mogens Hoegs gesandtskabsarkiver, Ordrer og breve m.m. 1648-55 (leaves stamped Ny kongl. Saml. Fol. 1299 e); Arkivalieronline unit 261583, images 77-93
documents.route: Peder Vibe (Copenhagen; later Bierreds and Flensborg) -> Peder Juel, Danish resident in Stockholm

plaintext.source: partial interlinear decipherment of the time on N. 319 (image 78), over about a third of its words; no other decipherment in the unit

transcription.source: Arkivalieronline images of unit 261583 (full size); images not reproduced
transcription.notes: 222 units = 149 cipher words in letters (split words joined) + 73 nomenclator code tokens (49 different numbers), counted at integration from transcription.txt and reading.md (the PR's table had 150 words and 75 codes for these letters; image 77 has 22 words, image 93 has 24 codes, and the code 545 on image 78 is now a C token). Transcribed number by number by the contributor's AI agents (11 Nov 2026); the held-out sets were transcribed and hashed before any decryption (frozen/working/transcr/); everything was re-read at native zoom after the measurements. At verification about 95 numbers of image 83 left agreed with the image. No human re-reading.

system.summary: Shift cipher with the shift chosen per word: each cipher word is an opener (1-3 or 24-39) giving a shift k (24-29 -> 0, 30-34 -> 1, 35-39 -> 2, 1-3 -> 3), then body numbers = rank of the letter + k in a 25-letter alphabet a...u w x y z ø, not cyclic; two- to four-digit nomenclator codes between the words; clear Danish between the cipher passages.
system.notes: Vibe announces the new alphabet in clear (image 62, 11 Jan 1649: 'dett ny Alphabet' is to be sent). Numbers are marked off by small ticks below the line; a word may be split in pieces with their own openers; 32/33/34 in the body stand for 1/2/3. 49 different code numbers, none identified and none shared with the old-cipher letters; in 1655 (N. 167) a new list runs to 1771. Nomenclator kinds are inferred from context only.

prior_solution.where: Partial interlinear decipherment of the time on N. 319 (image 78) only. Catalogue 2527 vetting (Daniel Bourdeau, 11 Nov 2026): DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry nothing. Fryxell 1836 gives a Swedish abstract of Juel's register of outgoing letters without the cipher passages. The contributor's web search of 11 Nov 2026 found no edition. Not searched again at verification or integration.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocol hashed before each single measurement; a partial reading may be published if explained). His AI agents transcribed, found the system, wrote and ran the protocols, read and wrote up. No human read the reading. At integration (12 Nov 2026) the project re-ran the scripts, split the target by key and recounted.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, system, protocols, measurements, reading, write-up)

solution.what: Cipher passages of images 77-93 transcribed number by number by the contributor's agents; the held-out sets hashed before any decryption; all re-read at native zoom afterwards.
System found on N. 319 (image 78) from the interlinear letters of the time: opener + body, body = rank + k, opener table 24-29 -> 0, 30-34 -> 1, 35-39 -> 2, 1-3 -> 3.

Test 1 (pre-registered; protocol hashed before the set was opened, by the contributor's record): one opener table for the whole unit, that of N. 319, 23-letter alphabet; held-out images 74 (N. 330), 77 (N. 316), 79 right (N. 334), 54 words, 335 numbers. M1 -3.068 against a best of 600 controls of -3.281: margin 0.21, under the bar of 0.30. FAILED; not measured again. Cause found afterwards: N. 330 is in the old cipher.

Test 2 (pre-registered after test 1 failed, with the rule changed: opener table learned on each letter, controls with the same optimisation): new held-out images 81, 83, 84, 87, 90 (55 words, 339 numbers, all in the new alphabet). M1 -2.713 against a best of 300 controls of -3.555: margin 0.841 over the bar of 0.30; readable Danish sentences. Passed. It validates the shift-per-word system, not a fixed table.

After the measurements: the alphabet found to have 25 letters with w and ø; openers that looked out of table shown to be word-division errors; the 11 letters or pages read with the one fixed table: 149 cipher words (132 certain, 14 probable, 1 restored, 2 unresolved); 73 nomenclator codes not identified.

Independent verification of PR #410 before integration: tests 1 and 2 re-run from frozen/ with the 11 archive.org corpus texts, identical figures including the learned tables; all frozen hashes match; a second decoder gives the same decryption; about 95 numbers of image 83 left agree with the transcription. Later controls, after the fact: the fixed new table with no fitting on held-out set 2 scores M1 -2.611 against a best control of -3.174 (margin 0.563); it scores -1.987 against a best of -2.568 for 200 random opener tables on the final transcription; the three images of test 1 scored separately give -3.980 vs -3.125 (image 74, old cipher), -2.353 vs -2.961 (77) and -2.632 vs -3.094 (79); a per-letter refit of k agrees with the fixed tables for 383 of 403 words of both ciphers.

Integration: target split by key (new alphabet here; the old cipher of 1649-1651 to vibejuel1649; the unsolved Krag letters of 1648 to a lead); eval() replaced by ast.literal_eval in scripts/decode.py with byte-identical output; counts taken again from the files (149 words, 73 code tokens; the PR had 150 and 75); the code 545 opening N. 319 made a C token; outcome.key set to partial, fraction_read 0.980, codes_open 73, read_share 0.595; validation restated (test 1 failed, test 2 on a changed rule validates the system only); reading read as sentences against the translation (grade B).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The system and the opener table were found on the one letter with a partial interlinear decipherment of the time (N. 319, image 78) and applied to every letter in the new alphabet; a pre-registered test of the shift-per-word system passed on five letters never opened before, after a first test had failed. The nomenclator is not recovered.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md: 146 of 149 cipher words in letters given a value (132 certain + 14 probable; 1 restored and 2 unresolved are holes) = 98.0%. The 73 nomenclator code tokens are counted apart (codes_open); with them as holes the read share is 146/222 = 65.8% (texts[].read_share).

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py). Test 1 FAILED: one opener table (that of N. 319) for the whole unit, M1 -3.068 against a best of 600 controls of -3.281, margin 0.21 under the bar of 0.30; one of its three held-out letters (N. 330) is in the old cipher. The rule was then changed (declared): test 2 learns the opener table on each letter; on five new-alphabet letters never opened (PROTOCOLE-2 SHA-256 62f533215e6f50db2f83079607851d27a68007e8821f46fff3076ab889d8ce4c) M1 -2.713 against a best of 300 controls of -3.555, margin 0.841: PASSED. Test 2 validates the shift-per-word system, not the fixed table of key.tsv. One word of image 87 had been deciphered mentally before the hash (declared). Both results reproduce exactly. Later control at verification, after the fact: the fixed table with no fitting on held-out set 2, M1 -2.611 against -3.174. Order of events by the contributor's record.

texts.label: Peder Vibe to Peder Juel, 1651-1655, cipher passages in the new alphabet of 11 letters or pages
texts.summary: Secret passages of Vibe's letters from Copenhagen, Bierreds and Flensborg, 1651 to May 1655: a seal of #876 to be copied from wax impressions; a servant debauched to get a packet of letters, and work to intercept letters of #872; #353 and #397 leaving for #770 with an instruction, and a border meeting (1653); Würtz said to be ennobled by #222; fireships built by #222; an opened letter of #879 (1654); a design that leaves the States General perplexed, and something to lie in the Sound (1655). The 49 code numbers that name the actors are not identified.

reading_review.by: Brice Dudout's AI agents; re-read at integration by an AI agent for the project
reading_review.note: Contributor: read as Danish sentences by AI agents only; no human read it. Integration (PR #410): reading.md read letter by letter against decryption.txt and translation.md; the cipher words construe with the clear words around them and the translation follows; but 73 code tokens stand for the persons and places, so who does what is mostly open; images 87 and 93 are fragments; 14 words are only probable, 1 restored, 2 unresolved: grade B, read in part. Not re-checked against the images at integration apart from the head of N. 319.

outcome.notes: Split by key on 12 Nov 2026 (one key, one entry): the old cipher of 1649-1651 is targets/vibejuel1649. frozen/ holds the files of both tests. No decipherment of these letters was known beyond the partial gloss of N. 319. Prior art was not searched again at verification or integration.
